title: A Jaunt in Japan
subtitle: Ninety Days’ Leave in the Far East
summary: Sydney Charles Fishburn Jackson (1863–1928), a captain of the Hampshire Regiment on the staff at Poona, spent his ninety days’ leave in 1899 on a journey to Japan with his wife. They sailed from Bombay on 9 March by a French mail steamer, by Colombo, Singapore and Saigon, to Hongkong, made a trip to Canton, and went on by Shanghai to Nagasaki and through the Inland Sea to Kobe.

In Japan they visited Osaka, Kioto, Nara, Lake Biwa and Nagoya, Yokohama and Tokio, Nikho and Chiuzenzi, and Miyanoshita and Hakone, and saw theatres, wrestlers, temples and a procession of the Emperor; they left Yokohama on 10 May. The preface says the book was written to answer the practical questions of travellers, and an appendix gives the costs of the journey.
